title: PXAPI shared definitions v1
description: Reusable $defs for the PXAPI v1 contracts. This file is not a contract: no document validates against it as a whole. Every definition here is referenced by at least one contract; nothing here carries analysis meaning of its own.

schema_version.description: The exact contract version a v1 document claims. Any other value is rejected; a later contract version is a new schema artifact, never a widened const.

id.description: An opaque, stable identifier: non-empty, at most 128 characters, no line breaks, no leading or trailing whitespace. No identifier technology (UUID, ULID, prefix scheme) is prescribed; the producer chooses and keeps it stable.

token.description: An opaque vocabulary token (channel, provider, source type, artifact type, kind). Its meaning is defined by the producer, not by this schema; the schema only fixes the lexical shape.

code.description: A stable machine-readable code in upper snake case (problem codes, failure codes, reason codes). Codes are open: a consumer must treat a code it does not know as a generic member of its category, never as an error.

timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 instant in UTC with the mandatory 'Z' designator, e.g. 2026-09-02T10:15:30Z or 2026-09-02T10:15:30.250Z. Numeric offsets, local times, lowercase designators and date-only values are rejected by the pattern, not by a format annotation.

url.description: An absolute http or https URL as a structural shape only. Reachability, canonicalisation and egress policy (loopback, private ranges, metadata endpoints) are not contract concerns and are enforced elsewhere.

text.description: Free text with at least one non-whitespace character, bounded; line breaks are allowed.

short_text.description: A single-line label, title or version string with at least one non-whitespace character, at most 200 characters.

language.description: A two-letter lowercase ISO 639-1 language code.

country.description: A two-letter uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

confidence.description: An integer confidence on the fixed scale 0..5. The scale carries no named levels in v1.

score_value.description: A score or index value on the closed interval 0..100. How the value is computed is not part of this contract.

assessment_state.description: Whether a subject was assessed at all. MEASURED: a deterministic measurement was taken. OBSERVED: a qualitative observation was recorded. NOT_ASSESSED: no assessment happened; the record explains why and carries no value. A missing assessment is never a finding about the website.

value_state.description: For an assessed subject: whether the assessment produced a value. UNKNOWN means the assessment ran but could not determine a value; it is explicit data with a reason, never a substitute value and never a negative finding.

not_assessed_reason.description: Why a subject was not assessed. Every value describes the analysis process, not the website: a provider failure, a runtime error, a missing permission, a timeout, an inapplicable metric or a metric that was not requested.

unknown_reason.description: Why an assessment produced no value. An open, stable reason code chosen by the producer (e.g. INDETERMINATE, CONFLICTING_OBSERVATIONS, UNPARSEABLE); the vocabulary is deliberately not closed in v1.

evidence_class.description: The authority of a statement, ordered HYPOTHESIS < SUPPORTED_INFERENCE < VERIFIED_FACT. An unknown is not an evidence class; it is expressed through value_state.

score_state.description: Whether an index or overall score was computed. NOT_SCORED carries a reason and no value; there is no partial or placeholder score in v1.

not_scored_reason.description: Why an index or overall score was not computed, as an open stable code (e.g. INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE, NOT_ASSESSED_INPUTS, POLICY_WITHHELD).

artifact_id.description: Required. The stable identifier of the referenced artifact.

artifact_type.description: Required. The producer-defined type of the referenced artifact. Contract names are the usual values, but rendered reports, raw provider payloads and chart data are valid artifact types too.

artifact_ref.description: A reference to an artifact by identity and type. Where the artifact is stored is not part of any v1 contract.

kind.description: Required. What kind of producer this was (e.g. model, tool, human, cache).

version.description: Required. The producer's version as the producer reports it.

producer_ref.description: What produced an artifact. Collectors, models and providers are interchangeable implementations behind this shape.

type.description: Required. The kind of subject (e.g. page, host, sitemap, query).

value.description: Required. The subject's stable value (e.g. a URL, a hostname, a query text).

subject.description: The stable subject a measurement or observation is about, so that later runs can be compared against it.

kind.description: Required. The kind of source (e.g. http_response, serp_snapshot, public_register, document).

value.description: Required. The source's stable locator or identity.

retrieved_at.description: Optional. When the source was retrieved. Absent means the source is not a retrieved resource (e.g. a constant or a register entry); an unknown retrieval time is not representable in v1.

source_ref.description: Where a statement or measurement comes from.

contract_name.description: The names of the v1 contracts: the eleven canonical contracts followed by the four support contracts. Kept in parity with contracts/v1/manifest.json by test.

run_state.description: The Analysis Run state vocabulary: the thirteen lifecycle states in order, then the six explicit failure states. Kept in parity with pxapi.domain.run_state.RunState by test.

stage.description: The processing activities of an Analysis Run in canonical order. A stage names what was executing; it is not a run state. Kept in parity with pxapi.domain.stage_execution.Stage by test.

stage_status.description: The execution status of one stage. CANCELLED is only ever the consequence of a concurrent sibling stage failing.

code.description: Required. A stable, client-readable failure code.

detail.description: Required. A single-line, bounded, client-safe explanation. Never a traceback, a filesystem path, a secret or a raw internal exception message.
